text: Theo pulls up the exact numbers Lessons 12 and 14 already established. Before the fix, eastus2-2 ran nearly pegged at 96 percent while the other two zones sat at a quarter of that, blending to a cluster-wide average of about 72 percent that looked completely fine.

After the fix, all three zones land within about a 2-point band of each other, each roughly half-utilized. That settles part of the argument: the fix already corrected the distribution problem, so more total capacity was never the missing piece. But 46 to 48 percent doesn't guarantee headroom for a bigger sale next quarter, and Casey's growth concern is still real.

The actual compromise: raise the sale-window ceiling from 12 to 16 replicas, enough to keep each zone at or below 60 percent even with 30 percent more traffic than this quarter's peak, paired with a permanent per-AZ spread guarantee and the existing off-hours minimum kept in place the rest of the year.

Casey gets real headroom calculated from the actual post-fix peak, for the exact window it's needed. Dana gets a defensible number for the budget review, backed by measured data instead of an argument won by whoever was more persuasive in the room.
